Analysis: Hypothesis 2 provides a more defined molecular target (miR-155 and IRF-8) than Hypothesis 1, which is broader and less specific with regard to the EV cargo components. This specificity in Hypothesis 2 increases its testability since experiments can be designed to measure miR-155 delivery and IRF-8 suppression, while the known role of IRF-8 in myeloid differentiation bolsters its overall plausibility. Although both hypotheses carry safety and mechanistic complexities, the greater clarity of a defined miRNA-target interaction in Hypothesis 2 makes it a more tractable starting point. Therefore, considering novelty (through its specific focus), plausibility, ease of testing, and a more targeted approach to potential therapeutic intervention, Hypothesis 2 is the superior option.
